ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The figure below is a double-reciprocal plot of one of the three types of reversible inhibition of enzymes; please determine which type of inhibition this is. \begin{center} \includegraphics[scale=0.5]{q_00349_001.png} \end{center}
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a double-reciprocal plot of enzyme kinetics, with the vertical axis labeled 1/v and the horizontal axis labeled 1/[S]. There are multiple straight lines in the figure, and the right side is labeled “normal” and “[I] increased,” indicating that when the inhibitor concentration increases, the slope of the straight line becomes larger. All straight lines intersect at the same point on the vertical axis, which is labeled 1/Vmax; the negative half of the horizontal axis marks the intercept under normal conditions, -1/Km, and the intercept that changes toward -1/[Km(1+[I]/Ki)], which is closer to the origin, in the presence of inhibitor. Then reason: The multiple straight lines have a common vertical-axis intercept 1/Vmax, indicating that Vmax is unchanged; while the horizontal-axis intercept changes, indicating that the apparent Km changes. In reversible inhibition, Vmax unchanged while Km changes is the typical double-reciprocal plot feature of competitive inhibition. Therefore this figure represents competitive inhibition.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：这是双倒数图，纵轴为1/v，横轴为1/[S]；随[I]加大，多条直线斜率增大，但都通过同一个纵轴截距1/Vmax，横轴截距按-Km相关项变化。再推理：共同的1/Vmax表示Vmax不变，而横截距变化表示表观Km改变；这种特征对应竞争性抑制。

method.model_answer: 竞争性抑制（Competitive suppression / competitive inhibition）

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the canonical Lineweaver–Burk diagnostic pattern: identical y-intercept with changing slope/x-intercept. This is the direct and essentially unique route for this image-grounded enzyme inhibition question.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the plot axes as 1/v versus 1/[S]. Observe that the normal line and inhibitor-added lines intersect at the same y-axis point labeled 1/Vmax, while increasing [I] makes the lines steeper and shifts the x-intercept from -1/Km toward -1/(Km(1+[I]/Ki)).
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to identify the task as classifying one of the reversible enzyme inhibition types from a double-reciprocal plot.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In Lineweaver–Burk plots, competitive inhibition leaves Vmax unchanged, increases apparent Km, preserves the y-intercept 1/Vmax, increases slope, and moves the x-intercept toward zero. Noncompetitive and uncompetitive inhibition have different intercept patterns.
